topic: Complete binary three-item target-law classification under MNAR conditional missingness DAGs.

open_problems.open_problem: Classify uniform target-law identification for every labelled binary three-item conditional-MNAR DAG by a total deterministic procedure returning either eight denominator-safe rational observed-law formulas or explicit strictly positive rational observational twins, with a graph-uniform operation bound.

source_refs.claim: The paper proves a complete graphical criterion for full-law identification but leaves complete characterization of target-law identification open.
source_refs.author: Razieh Nabi, Rohit Bhattacharya, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: The intervention-tree procedure is constructive and sound but not complete; its documented failure includes a graph rescued by odds-ratio factorization.
source_refs.author: Anna Guo, Razieh Nabi

source_refs.claim: Grouped partial-order fixing and induced selection subproblems identify target laws missed by earlier procedures, but do not give a complete target-law criterion.
source_refs.author: Rohit Bhattacharya, Razieh Nabi, Ilya Shpitser, James M. Robins

source_refs.excerpt: The run proved a sound pointwise response-function/CAD decision theorem on the finite
delayed collider selection destroys the CADMG Markov invariant required for confluence

open_problems.why_unsolved: Full-law completeness does not settle target-law identification because p_X can remain recoverable when response-kernel components are not. Published target-law methods cover complementary sufficient regimes: grouped fixing and intervention trees can miss odds-ratio rescues, while odds-ratio arguments do not subsume every fixing derivation. The closest prior CausalSmith classifier obtained only a pointwise response-fiber/CAD oracle and found that context restriction can destroy the Markov invariant needed for fixing-order confluence. The missing work is therefore a graph-factorization-preserving finite dichotomy for all positive laws, including exceptional rank strata, rather than an unaudited enumeration or a generic algebraic decision oracle.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sound-and-complete Complete3 theorem with an explicit finite operation bound, eight rational functionals whose divisors are observed marginals positive throughout each ID graph model, and two positive rational 64-cell Markov laws agreeing on all 27 coarsened cells for each NONID graph.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation links graph-specific recovery directly to an executable identification workflow and ends at the incompleteness of intervention-only search.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: MNAR graphs encode exploitable restrictions -> intervention sequences expose selection propagation -> intervention trees return constructive formulas but miss odds-ratio rescues -> a finite hybrid must decide every binary K=3 graph

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over grouped and partial-order fixing in observed kernels, including induced selection subproblems, together with a derivation trace for each recovered target cell.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These are the strongest published intervention-style transformations available for a finite K=3 search.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the Chen odds-ratio factorization and the full-law obstruction proof, replacing full-law recovery by a target-cell-specific fibre analysis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies both the known algebraic rescue mechanism and the closest completeness-proof template, while explicitly separating full-law from target-law identification.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the odds-ratio observed-data influence-function derivation and augmented inverse-probability construction to classifier-returned target-law functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest limit-theory companion for functionals recovered through the same odds-ratio parameterization.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a finite minimal-obstruction catalogue for nonidentification of the binary three-item target law in which every terminal obstruction yields a reusable strictly positive rational twin family and every nonidentified labelled graph reduces to a catalogue member.

source_refs.claim: Self-censoring and colluding paths form a complete obstruction catalogue for the full law, but are not necessary obstructions for target-law identification.
source_refs.author: Razieh Nabi, Rohit Bhattacharya, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: The colluder argument constructs observationally equivalent full laws, while the paper also exhibits target laws that survive colluders.
source_refs.author: Rohit Bhattacharya, Razieh Nabi, Ilya Shpitser, James M. Robins

source_refs.claim: The criss-cross MNAR analysis provides a model-specific observational-equivalence construction but not a finite positive rational basis for every binary K=3 failure.
source_refs.author: Anna Guo, Jiwei Zhao, Razieh Nabi

source_refs.excerpt: Strengthen the universal hedge handle into an explicit witness-extraction algorithm from a terminal obstruction
Replace the unrestricted global response-law simplex with a latent-DAG or district-factorized response-type construction

open_problems.why_unsolved: The full-law obstruction theorem cannot be inherited because target laws may survive a colluder. Prior completeness attempts also perturbed ambient response-law simplexes whose points need not factorize according to the claimed graph. For conditional MNAR, the first changed proof step is a graph-factorized rational parameterization enforcing equality of all 27 coarsened cells, followed by a positivity-preserving rational direction that changes a named p_X cell. The presolve's self-censoring and criss-cross twins cover large regions, but no lifting theorem or residual catalogue proves that every failed fixing trace has such a rational interior witness.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite list of minimal K=3 obstruction templates, a rationally parameterized positive twin map for each template, and a reduction/lifting theorem that turns every nonidentifying terminal trace into two explicit same-observed/different-target 64-cell tables.

writing_exemplar.why: It is the clearest model for turning local graphical obstructions and explicit paired laws into a global completeness frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Algorithmic failure alone does not prove nonidentification -> local structures admit indistinguishable model pairs -> closure of those structures proves full-law completeness -> target-law completeness needs a finer positive rational obstruction basis

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the hedge-to-paired-SCM construction so observed contributions cancel while one target coordinate changes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested compiler is the positivity- and coarsening-strengthened analogue of the classical necessity proof for ID.

method_exemplars.technique: Synchronize multiple available distributions using strictly positive conditional probabilities while retaining a separating target contrast.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The 27 coarsened-cell equalities are simultaneous exact data constraints whose graph-compatible positive realization is the central witness problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use exact finite response-function polynomial feasibility to locate separated compatible models, then decode each successful computation into a rational analytic certificate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides an independent audit oracle for proposed positive twin families even though quantifier elimination is excluded from the final completeness proof.

open_problems.open_problem: Separate graph-uniform target-law identification from rank-generic or dependence-conditioned identification in binary three-item colluder models, including every strictly positive rank-degenerate stratum.

source_refs.claim: Categorical colluders can regain full-law identification under additional categorical-colluder independences and matrix full-rank conditions; rank failure yields nonidentification.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka, Juha Karvanen

source_refs.claim: Multivariate self-censoring is identified under a completeness condition that becomes a matrix full-rank condition for discrete variables.
source_refs.author: Yilin Li, Wang Miao, Ilya Shpitser, Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Criss-cross MNAR is nonparametrically nonidentified, while added exponential-family and rank restrictions provide sufficient restricted-model identification.
source_refs.author: Anna Guo, Jiwei Zhao, Razieh Nabi

open_problems.why_unsolved: The graph-uniform question quantifies over every strictly positive law Markov to the DAG. A formula requiring a determinant or contrast that can vanish at an interior Markov law therefore proves only generic or restricted-model identification. The categorical-colluder, multivariate self-censoring, and criss-cross results recover laws after adding rank, completeness, or parametric structure, but do not decide the unrestricted graph model on the exceptional positive strata. The first unresolved step is to determine whether each rank collapse admits a separate denominator-safe formula or an exact positive twin fibre.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite stratum-by-stratum theorem for each binary K=3 colluder graph proving either one observed-marginal rational functional valid on the whole positive graph model or a strictly positive rank-degenerate twin fibre, with generic-only recovery labelled separately.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the exact tension between a graphical colluder obstruction and identification restored by finite categorical rank.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Colluders obstruct unrestricted recovery -> finite category counts yield matrix equations -> uniqueness depends on matrix rank -> uniform graphical identification requires resolving every positive rank-degenerate stratum

method_exemplars.technique: Translate colluder equations into finite matrices, prove uniqueness at full column rank, and construct nonidentification at rank failure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Binary three-item response models produce exactly the finite conditional-probability matrices whose exceptional strata need audit.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce odds-factor recovery to injectivity of a Fredholm equation and, in the discrete case, to finite matrix completeness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It makes explicit the first proof step that breaks when a missingness identification argument reaches a rank-degenerate law.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over conditional-likelihood and estimating-equation inference for identifiable odds-ratio parameters in criss-cross MNAR models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies limit theory for the nearest colluder setting and keeps generic/restricted identification distinct from uniform graphical recovery.

open_problems.open_problem: For positive binary three-item conditional-MNAR DAGs, does uniform identification of p_X always imply an eight-cell rational functional with only universally positive observed-marginal divisors, or can an identified target be necessarily algebraic but non-rational?

source_refs.excerpt: Restricting successful outputs to rational expressions could be false
a terminating global real-algebraic identification oracle with exact countermodels on failure

open_problems.why_unsolved: A prior finite-SCM project records the concrete warning that a polynomial model can identify a unique algebraic but non-rational function, so finite decidability alone cannot justify Complete3's rational-output grammar. The first proof step that changes is to exploit the special triangular binary response-kernel factorization and the 27-cell coarsening map to show that singleton target fibres lie in the rational function field localized only at universally positive observed marginals. If that field-membership claim fails, Complete3's requested output type is false even though point identification may hold.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a rational-generation theorem for every uniformly identified three-item target cell with an explicit allowed denominator set, or one positive labelled graph and observed-law family proving that its uniquely identified target is an unavoidable non-rational algebraic root.

writing_exemplar.why: Its finite polynomial formulation cleanly separates point identification from the representation of the identifying map.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Finite SCM compatibility is polynomial -> singleton target fibres establish point identification -> singleton algebraic roots need not be rational functions -> characterize the function field forced by binary conditional missingness

method_exemplars.technique: Use elimination ideals and generic-versus-global identifiability to test whether a target coordinate belongs to the rational function field of observed coordinates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired dichotomy is a rational-field-membership question for the image of the coarsening map.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode the finite response-function model polynomially and certify singleton fibres, including exceptional positive strata.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the exact algebraic model on which rationality must be proved or refuted.

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate recursively generated identifying functionals and derive asymptotically linear estimators on positive regular submodels.
method_exemplars.why_closest: If rational generation holds, this architecture supplies the estimator rung; an algebraic-root branch identifies exactly where it must change.

open_problems.open_problem: Give a canonical terminating normal form and explicit worst-case operation bound for a hybrid binary three-item search combining intervention-tree pruning, grouped fixing, conditional-independence substitutions, and odds-ratio rescue.

source_refs.claim: The paper supplies valid grouped partial-order fixing schedules but does not provide an efficient complete schedule search.
source_refs.author: Rohit Bhattacharya, Razieh Nabi, Ilya Shpitser, James M. Robins

source_refs.claim: The intervention tree gives an executable sound search with known odds-ratio rescue failures, not a canonical complete state space.
source_refs.author: Anna Guo, Razieh Nabi

source_refs.claim: Nested-Markov fixing proves sequence-invariance for reachable kernels after valid fixing sets are established, but not for context-restricted hybrid MNAR operations.
source_refs.author: Thomas S. Richardson, Robin J. Evans, James M. Robins, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.excerpt: The adjacent-swap lemma is local and does not claim that context restriction commutes with fixing
including a bound on response-map size and certificate-verification complexity

open_problems.why_unsolved: Intervention trees, grouped fixing, and odds-ratio reconstruction use different state objects. Ordinary nested-fixing sequence invariance begins only after a valid fixing set is known, while the prior lm-graph run found that context restriction need not commute with fixing and can destroy the needed Markov invariant. The first changed proof step is therefore a pattern-indexed trace invariant specifying when each kernel operation is licensed, followed by adjacent-operation identities or explicit noncommutation witnesses. Without that invariant, the unaudited 48-graph residual cannot establish sound coverage or a legitimate operation bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-state transition system with a pattern-indexed soundness invariant, a canonicalization theorem for successful traces, a decreasing termination measure, and an explicit bound B on state transitions, rational operations, and certificate checks for all 12,800 inputs.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates why simple sequential fixing is insufficient and formulates the destination in terms of grouped partial orders and induced selection subproblems.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sequential fixing misses recoverable MNAR graphs -> grouped operations and projected subproblems recover more -> unrestricted schedules lack a complete efficient search -> binary K=3 permits a canonical bounded hybrid state space

method_exemplars.technique: Use intervention trees to represent candidate response-indicator interventions and explicitly propagate and prune induced selection sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is already an executable state representation for the principal fixing branch; the first extension is to add grouped-fixing and odds-ratio states.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the adjacent-swap proof of fixing-sequence invariance to kernels carrying explicit missingness-pattern provenance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Sequence invariance is the natural lemma for quotienting syntactically different search branches into canonical states.

method_exemplars.technique: Compile a successful intervention-tree trace into recursive inverse-probability estimating equations and sandwich-style large-sample inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows that canonical search traces can carry executable estimator information rather than only symbolic identification.

open_problems.open_problem: Compile every rational Complete3 ID certificate into the joint multinomial influence function of the eight-cell plug-in target estimator, a consistent possibly singular covariance estimator, and a simultaneous confidence region uniform on each fixed epsilon-interior graph model.

source_refs.claim: After the full-law identification result, the paper identifies estimation theory for functionals of the recovered law as further work.
source_refs.author: Razieh Nabi, Rohit Bhattacharya, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: The intervention-tree work develops recursive parametric IPW inference but leaves influence-function-based and more flexible estimation as an open direction.
source_refs.author: Anna Guo, Razieh Nabi

source_refs.claim: The paper gives an efficiency bound and augmented inverse-probability estimator for target functionals under a no-self-censoring odds-ratio model, not arbitrary classifier-returned rational formulas.
source_refs.author: Daniel Malinsky, Ilya Shpitser, Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: Estimation, graph learning, continuous variables, nonpositive support, and finite-sample inference are outside the core
every branch guard and active algebraic operation is separated from its singular boundary

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing influence-function results are attached to particular no-self-censoring, pattern-graph, or parametric intervention-tree models, while the nearest prior classifier left estimation outside scope. Complete3 may return many graph-specific rational maps of one 27-cell multinomial vector, and no located source supplies their automatic joint eight-coordinate inference. The concrete missing step is a syntax-directed derivative proof respecting the simplex constraint and every formula-specific divisor; uniformity requires an epsilon lower bound for all active observed marginals, and the covariance procedure must remain valid when the eight-cell target covariance has the unavoidable probability-simplex singularity or additional graph-induced degeneracy.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For every Complete3 ID trace f_G(q), an explicit influence vector Df_G(q)(e_O-q), a consistent plug-in covariance matrix without invertibility assumptions, and a simultaneous eight-cell Wald, max-t, or projected Gaussian region with uniform asymptotic coverage on each fixed epsilon-interior subclass.

writing_exemplar.why: It connects constructive graph-specific identification directly to estimators and explicitly motivates a more general inference layer.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A graph-specific derivation yields computable formulas -> estimators should mirror the derivation -> current recursive IPW theory covers only selected mechanisms -> every classifier-generated rational target needs automatic joint uncertainty quantification

method_exemplars.technique: Project a full-data influence function into the observed-data tangent space under an odds-ratio factorization and estimate its variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the closest influence-function proof for target functionals recovered by Complete3's odds-ratio branches.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine response-pattern-specific influence contributions to obtain semiparametric efficiency and multiply robust estimation under nonmonotone missingness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its observed data use the same finite missingness-pattern coarsening and show how pattern contributions enter one influence function.

method_exemplars.technique: Recursively differentiate fixing-based sums, products, and kernel divisions and prove asymptotic linearity for the compiled estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Complete3's successful traces use the same algebraic primitives, now over a finite 27-cell multinomial law.

literature_map:
Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (ICML 2020, arXiv:2004.04872) give necessary and sufficient graphical conditions for full-law recovery, while target-law completeness remains open.
Bhattacharya, Nabi, Shpitser, and Robins (UAI 2020, arXiv:1907.00241) introduce grouped partial-order fixing and induced selection subproblems; the resulting target-law procedure is sufficient rather than complete.
Guo and Nabi (2026 working paper) introduce intervention trees and the flexMissing workflow, tracking induced and propagated selection and compiling successes into recursive estimators.
That intervention-tree procedure is explicitly sound but incomplete; its documented rejection of an odds-ratio-recoverable graph shows why a hybrid calculus is needed.
Chen (Biometrics 2007, doi:10.1111/j.1541-0420.2006.00701.x) provides the odds-ratio parameterization used by later MNAR identification and inference work.
Tikka and Karvanen (2024, arXiv:2402.05633) recover categorical-colluder full laws under finite matrix conditions, creating a sharp generic-versus-uniform rank issue.
Li, Miao, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (Biometrics 2023, arXiv:2207.08535) identify multivariate self-censoring models under statistical completeness, which becomes full matrix rank for discrete variables.
Guo, Zhao, and Nabi (UAI 2023, arXiv:2306.06443) show criss-cross MNAR nonparametric failure alongside partial recovery and restricted parametric identification.
Shpitser (NeurIPS 2016) and Sadinle and Reiter (Biometrika 2017, doi:10.1093/biomet/asw063) establish the no-self-censoring and itemwise-conditionally-independent substrate.
Nabi and Bhattacharya (UAI 2023, PMLR 216) study testable implications of missing-data DAGs; testability does not supply target-law completeness.
Malinsky, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (JASA 2022, arXiv:1909.01848) derive efficiency bounds and augmented inverse-probability inference for no-self-censoring models.
Chen (Annals of Statistics 2022, arXiv:2004.00744) develops pattern-graph identification, efficiency theory, and multiply robust estimation for nonmonotone missingness.
Richardson, Evans, Robins, and Shpitser (Annals of Statistics 2023, arXiv:1701.06686) prove fixing-sequence invariance for reachable nested-Markov kernels, a candidate tool for canonicalizing hybrid states.
de Aguas, Henckel, Pensar, and Biele (UAI 2025, PMLR 286) add missingness-specific context and mechanism shifts with recovery criteria, but address a broader labelled model rather than binary K=3 target-law completeness.
The public March 2026 talk listing describes partial solutions and remaining failure modes, and the bounded search found no public theorem classifying all 12,800 labelled K=3 graphs with rational formulas or positive rational twins.
